newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU Commission will discuss tobacco policy.
newsitem.headline: EU Commission will discuss tobacco policy.

text.p: The European Commission will debate on Wednesday the increasingly controversial question of its one-billion-Ecu annual subsidies to European Union tobacco growers, EU Commissioner Franz Fischler said on Monday.
"This is an issue of principle. We will not be discussing how to reform the tobacco sector. It is (to be) a debate about principle," he told a news conference.
The Commission faces several alternatives in its approach to subsidising tobacco growers -- mainly in the Mediterranean regions of the EU.
Although the cost of subsidies has fallen slightly it still costs the EU farm budget about one billion Ecus per year.
"Firstly, if we stop production, which will cost us 100,000 jobs, farmers will have to be found other jobs or we can try to find a programme which perhaps concentrates on quality," Fischler said.
The Commission has been facing increasing criticism in recent weeks over the apparent conflict between its policy of subsidising tobacco growers and its 25-million-Ecu anti-cancer campaign.

EU farmers who grow black tobacco, which is exported mainly to Eastern Europe and Africa, grow it on small plots averaging one hectare and have no alternative crops, a Commission official said. -- Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6800
